نَبْذٌ (tropical:) A little; a small quantity; (S, A, L, K;) مِنَ المَالِ of wealth, or property; (S, A, L;) as also ↓ نُبْذَةٌ [which is a word much used though I find it explained in few lexicons]; (L, TA;) because what is little is thrown away, and disregarded: (A:) and in like manner, of herbage, and of rain, and of hoariness or hoary hair, (S, A, L,) &c: (L:) and a small number of men: (A, L:) and the latter word, a piece, or portion, of a thing, such as a perfume: (L:) pl. of the former, أَنْبَاذٌ: (L, K:) [and of the latter, نُبَذٌ.] ―
-b2- أَنْبَاذٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ (K, * TA) (tropical:) The refuse of the people; (TA;) mixed people of the baser sort. (K, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
